scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of the default branch (depth 20), so has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy; the repo has a single commit. Single-file Python CLI (artwork.py, 1101 lines) read in full for subprocess usage, file writes and XML parsing. The raw 'SQL write ops: 1' hit is a false positive (no database code exists). Docs (README, INDEX, QUICK_REFERENCE, FEATURE_EXAMPLES, CONSOLIDATION_SUMMARY) were used for purpose only.

gitignore_gaps: no .env, *.pem, *.key or credentials.json patterns (none present; the tool uses no secrets)

findings: no requirements.txt or pyproject.toml; Pillow is an optional third-party import (PIL, guarded by try/except) documented only in README as 'pip install Pillow'
external programs invoked and not declared in any manifest: Inkscape, ImageMagick (montage), optional svgo and scour

entry_points.framework: argparse (subcommands convert, colors, montage, palette, style guide, optimize)

file_system_access.detail: reads vector and image files from a user-supplied directory (default current working directory), recursively by default
writes converted files, color lists, palettes (JSON/CSS), HTML style guides and optimized SVGs to output paths (open(...,'w') at lines 235, 458, 462, 473, 569, 843)

runs external programs via subprocess.run with argument lists (no shell=True): inkscape (lines 71, 94), ImageMagick montage (line 306), svgo/scour (lines 516, 539); paths and options come from command-line arguments and interactive prompts
hardcoded Inkscape install locations under C:\\Program Files and scoop, /usr/bin, /opt (lines 32-39) used only to locate the program

what_this_app_can_do: Batch-converts vector files (SVG, PDF, EPS, AI and others) to other formats by calling Inkscape on files in a chosen folder tree.
Extracts hex color values from SVG files, and generates color palettes from images or SVGs as JSON, CSS or palette files.
Builds image contact-sheet montages by calling ImageMagick.
Generates HTML style guides and optimizes SVG files using svgo, scour or built-in compression.

data_sources_touched.source: Local image and vector files in user-chosen directories
Output files written to user-chosen locations (converted images, JSON/CSS, HTML, SVG)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Runs only as a command-line tool by whoever executes it on their own machine; no network listener and no authentication.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: none found - no credentials, no network calls and no external data flows; the tool executes locally installed programs (Inkscape, ImageMagick, svgo, scour) with file names derived from the scanned folder
